Cases.What: SELECT the file once in Explorer (single click). Do not open it.
Cases.Why: Control: does merely browsing/selecting update Access?

Cases.What: DOUBLE-CLICK the file to open it in Notepad, then close Notepad.
Cases.Why: The commonest real-world "user accessed a file".

Cases.What: Press F2 and rename the file to  renamed_explorer_<caseid>.txt
Cases.Why: CLI rename does not update Access on 25H2. Does Explorer differ?

Cases.What: Ctrl+C on the file, then Ctrl+V in the DESTINATION folder.
Ctrl+X on the file, then Ctrl+V in the DESTINATION folder.
DRAG the file to the DESTINATION folder. Same volume, so this moves.
Ctrl+X on the file, then Ctrl+V in the DESTINATION folder on the OTHER volume.
Cases.Why: THE CRITICAL CASE. The 22H2 charts show $SI Creation INHERITED here but set to move time via CLI -- the only cell where mechanism changes the answer.

Cases.What: Hold SHIFT and DRAG the file to the DESTINATION folder on the OTHER volume (Shift forces a move).
Cases.Why: Cross-volume drag defaults to COPY; Shift forces a move. Does it match cut/paste?

Cases.What: DRAG the file to the DESTINATION folder on the OTHER volume, WITHOUT Shift. This copies.
Cases.Why: Cross-volume drag is a copy. Does it match a same-volume copy?

Cases.What: Press DELETE (not Shift+Delete). The file goes to the Recycle Bin.
Cases.Why: Recycle is a move into $Recycle.Bin plus a rename to $R... -- NOT the same as shift+delete.

Cases.What: Press SHIFT+DELETE and confirm. Permanent delete.
Cases.Why: Should match the CLI delete rules.
